mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has shown a net recovery trend over the past four weeks (from -18.3 to -15.9), signaling a gradual return of commuting routines. This sustained easing of work-from-home behavior is expected to raise weekday retail footfall and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days in more than half of historical instances where WORKPLACES showed net four-week improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly improvement in TRANSIT mobility (less negative than the prior week) reflects a surge in out-of-home travel that typically precedes a rebound in retail visits within two weeks, as commuters and shoppers resume transit-based outings.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change improves by more than 4 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -25.0 at t-1w to -20.7 at t-0w, a 4.3 point improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within the subsequent two weeks despite TRANSIT crossing the +4 point weekly improvement threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility both increase in the same week, they jointly indicate a restored commuting pattern that compounds to lift retail footfall more strongly than either series alone, producing a higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks despite simultaneous weekly gains in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: In the current post-state-of-emergency easing regime, persistently low RESIDENTIAL mobility alongside recovering PARKS and TRANSIT indicates that relaxed restrictions continue to hold, encouraging households to resume leisure and shopping outings, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays below 8 and PARKS/TRANSIT remain above their t-3w levels.

mechanism_narrative: The decision date falls in mid-November, the start of Tokyo's pre-holiday and year-end shopping season. This seasonal calendar effect independently drives increased discretionary retail visits regardless of short-term mobility noise, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-11-15, entering the pre-holiday shopping season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat through early December despite entering the seasonal shopping period.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below the +7.5 percentage-point level, it signals a short-term behavioral shift away from home-dwelling toward outside activity, which should translate into a near-immediate boost in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +7.5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL registered 7.7 at t-0w, near the 7.5 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL reading below +7.5.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp spike in PARKS mobility at t-1w (-1.7) followed by a partial reversal at t-0w (-10.4) suggests a transient outdoor-leisure substitution event, such as autumn foliage viewing, that diverted discretionary trips away from retail; as this effect fades, RETAIL_REC growth stalls or softens over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week and then reverses downward the following week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -18.3 to -14.4 to -1.7 to -10.4 over the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises steadily over the next two weeks despite the observed PARKS spike-and-reversal pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from 3.0 to 1.0) and failure of WORKPLACES to sustain its recovery (dropping to -22.9 before partially rebounding) together signal weakening economic activity and policy support, leading consumers to pull back on both essential and discretionary spending, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM declines for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES fails to sustain a positive trend
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 3.0 to 2.7 to 1.0 across the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite continued GROCERY_PHARM decline and WORKPLACES stagnation.
